root_cause_label: Persistent ELF VMA vs. File-Offset Confusion Blocked Constant Extraction
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly sought to read .rodata constants using the ELF virtual address (0x480000) as a file offset instead of the correct file offset (0x00080000), preventing any extraction of the exact floating-point rendering parameters needed to replicate the ray tracer, ultimately forcing the agent to submit a guessed approximation.
t_err_evidence: At step 49 the agent writes extract.py seeking to 0x480000 (the .rodata VMA) as if it were a file offset, reading zero bytes; the correct file offset from readelf output shown at step 57 is 0x00080000. This same error is repeated in over a dozen subsequent scripts (steps 50, 53-56, 58-60, 83-84, 90-103).
t_commit_evidence: At step 86 the agent abandons binary constant extraction entirely and writes ray2.c with manually guessed scene parameters (sphere center (0,-0.2,-3), radius 0.5, ground at y=-1, approximated sky gradient), locking in the approach of submitting an approximate implementation rather than an exact replica.
t_surface_evidence: At step 89 the agent runs its prototype ray tracer and observes output pixels (153 162 177) that differ from the known correct values (159 197 255) for pixel (0,0), providing the first observable signal that the implementation is wrong.
trigger_explanation: The agent did not know that ELF virtual memory addresses (VMAs) as reported by objdump/readelf section headers are not raw file offsets. Specifically, it confused .rodata VMA 0x480000 with the actual file offset 0x00080000. Every constant-extraction script read from the wrong location, returning empty bytes, and the agent never corrected this even after seeing readelf output clearly showing separate VMA and file-offset columns.
forewarning_evidence: At step 50, the first constant-extraction script (extract.py) produces absolutely no output despite running without error, signaling that the reads are returning no usable data. This pattern repeats across steps 54, 56, 59, 91-94, 101-103, all yielding empty output.
